import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The symbol length of $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$

For a field $F$ and $\ell \ge 1$, the Milnor K-group $K^M_n(F)/\ell$ is generated by the symbols
$\{a_1, \dots, a_n\}$ with $a_i \in F^\times$, and the *symbol length* of a class is the least
number of symbols in a decomposition of the class as a sum of symbols. The symbol length of
$K^M_n(F)/\ell$ is the supremum of the symbol lengths of its classes. When $\ell$ is invertible
in $F$, the norm residue isomorphism theorem (the Bloch–Kato conjecture, [Voevodsky2011]) gives
$K^M_n(F)/\ell \cong H^n(F, \mu_\ell^{\otimes n})$, so this is also the symbol length of Galois
cohomology.

The **symbol length problem** asks, for a given field $F$ and integers $n$ and $\ell$, for a $k$
such that the symbol length of every class in $K^M_n(F)/\ell$ is at most $k$, for example in
terms of a dimension of the field. That a class is a sum of *some* number of symbols is part of
the presentation of $K^M_n(F)$ recalled above, so the content lies entirely in the bound. In
degree $2$, over a field containing a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity, Merkurjev and Suslin's
theorem [MerkurjevSuslin1983] that the norm residue map is an isomorphism identifies
$K^M_2(F)/\ell$ with the $\ell$-torsion of the Brauer group and symbols with symbol algebras of
degree $\ell$; that is the form in which the question is usually studied, namely how many symbol
algebras are needed to represent a central simple algebra of exponent $\ell$. Becher and Hoffmann
[BecherHoffmann2004] named the invariant $\lambda_p$ in that degree and asked it for exactly the
fields considered below (their Question 4.6). The general form stated here is Problem 2.1.3.12 of
Krashen's PCMI notes; Krashen notes there that over complex function fields in at least three
variables no bound is known beyond Matzri's in degree $2$ and the case of $\ell$ a power of $2$,
which comes from the theory of quadratic forms, and that very little is known in degree $3$ and
higher [Krashen2024, §2.1.3.4].

This file states the problem for the rational function fields $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$ and
a prime $\ell = p$: determine the symbol length of $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$ as a
function of $m$, $n$ and $p$, where the symbol length is infinite if there is no bound.

What is known:
* in degree $0$ every symbol is the empty product $1$, so $K^M_0(F)/p = \mathbb{Z}/p$ has symbol
  length $p - 1$ for every field $F$;
* in degree $1$ every class of $K^M_1(F)/p = F^\times/(F^\times)^p$ is a single symbol, so the
  symbol length is at most $1$;
* $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$ has cohomological dimension $m$ [Serre1997, Ch. II, §4.2], so
  $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p = 0$ for $n > m$ and the symbol length is $0$;
* $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$ is a $C_m$ field (Tsen–Lang, [Lang1952]), so by Matzri's theorem
  [Matzri2016, Theorem 8.2] every class in $K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p^t$ is a sum of
  at most $t(p^{m-1} - 1)$ symbols when $m \ge 1$;
* in degree $2$ a tensor product of $m - 1$ symbol algebras of degree $p$ over
  $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$ can be a division algebra, so the symbol length is at least
  $m - 1$ for $m \ge 1$ [BecherHoffmann2004, Proposition 4.5], by an argument going back to
  Nakayama.

In degree $2$, Becher and Hoffmann ask whether that lower bound is the answer, that is whether
the symbol length is exactly $m - 1$ [BecherHoffmann2004, Question 4.6]. For $m = n = 2$, the
smallest case not settled above, this asks whether every class of
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, x_2))/p$ is a single symbol; they call it "a striking open question" and
note that it holds for $p \le 3$ by a theorem of Artin [BecherHoffmann2004, Introduction]. Since
$m - 1$ does not involve $p$, their question is an instance of the expectation recorded in
[Krashen2024, §2.1.3.4] that a bound can be taken independent of $\ell$. See also the survey
[Krashen2016].

The definitions `MilnorK`, `MilnorK.symbol`, `MilnorK.grade` and `MilnorK.symbolLengthBounds`
are in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/FieldTheory/MilnorKTheory.lean`.

*References:*
- [Krashen2024] D. Krashen, *PCMI Summer School (not quite) notes*, notes for the minicourse
  *Field arithmetic and the complexity of algebraic objects*, PCMI Graduate Summer School on
  Motivic Homotopy Theory, 2024, draft of 24 July 2024,
  [pdf](https://www.ias.edu/sites/default/files/pcmi-2024-07-24%20krashen.pdf).
- [BecherHoffmann2004] K. J. Becher and D. W. Hoffmann, *Symbol lengths in Milnor $K$-theory*,
  Homology Homotopy Appl. 6 (2004), no. 1, 17–31,
  [doi:10.4310/HHA.2004.v6.n1.a3](https://doi.org/10.4310/HHA.2004.v6.n1.a3).
- [MerkurjevSuslin1983] A. S. Merkurjev and A. A. Suslin, *K-cohomology of Severi–Brauer
  varieties and the norm residue homomorphism*, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 46 (1982),
  1011–1046; English translation Math. USSR-Izv. 21 (1983), no. 2, 307–340,
  [doi:10.1070/IM1983v021n02ABEH001793](https://doi.org/10.1070/IM1983v021n02ABEH001793).
- [Krashen2016] D. Krashen, *Period and index, symbol lengths, and generic splittings in Galois
  cohomology*, Bull. London Math. Soc. 48 (2016), 985–1000,
  [doi:10.1112/blms/bdw060](https://doi.org/10.1112/blms/bdw060).
- [Matzri2016] E. Matzri, *Symbol length in the Brauer group of a field*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.
  368 (2016), 413–427, [doi:10.1090/tran/6326](https://doi.org/10.1090/tran/6326),
  [arXiv:1402.0332](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0332).
- [Lang1952] S. Lang, *On quasi algebraic closure*, Ann. of Math. (2) 55 (1952), 373–390,
  [doi:10.2307/1969785](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969785).
- [Serre1997] J.-P. Serre, *Galois cohomology*, Springer Monographs in Mathematics, Springer,
  1997, [doi:10.1007/978-3-642-59141-9](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-59141-9).
- [Voevodsky2011] V. Voevodsky, *On motivic cohomology with Z/l-coefficients*, Ann. of Math. (2)
  174 (2011), 401–438,
  [doi:10.4007/annals.2011.174.1.11](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2011.174.1.11).
-/

open MilnorK

namespace SymbolLengthMilnorKTheory

/--
**The symbol length problem** for complex rational function fields [Krashen2024, Problem 2.1.3.12
and §2.1.3.4]: determine, as a function of $m$, $n$ and the prime $p$, the symbol length of
$K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$, that is the least $k$ such that every class is a sum of at
most $k$ symbols, or $\infty$ if there is no such $k$. The answer `sl m n p : ℕ∞` is
characterised by: `k` is such a bound if and only if `sl m n p ≤ k`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem :
    let sl : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ∞ := answer(sorry)
    ∀ m n p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ k : ℕ,
      k ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n ↔ sl m n p ≤ k := by
  sorry

/--
The symbol length problem in the form of [Krashen2024, Problem 2.1.3.12]: is there, for every
$m$, $n$ and prime $p$, a bound $k$ such that every class in $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$
is a sum of at most $k$ symbols?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.bounded :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ m n p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      (symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n).Nonempty := by
  sorry

/--
The expectation recorded in [Krashen2024, §2.1.3.4] that the bound can be taken independent of
the prime: is there, for every $m$ and every $n \ge 1$, a $k$ such that every class in
$K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$ is a sum of at most $k$ symbols for every prime $p$?
Degree $0$ is excluded because $K^M_0(F)/p = \mathbb{Z}/p$ has symbol length $p - 1$
(`symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_zero`), which is not bounded independently of $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.uniform :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ m n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      k ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n := by
  sorry

/--
The degree-$0$ case of `symbol_length_problem`: $K^M_0(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p = \mathbb{Z}/p$
has symbol length $p - 1$, since every symbol of degree $0$ is the empty product $1$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_zero (m p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsLeast (symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 0) (p - 1) :=
  isLeast_symbolLengthBounds_zero _ p hp.pos

/--
The degree-$1$ case of `symbol_length_problem`: every class of
$K^M_1(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p = F^\times/(F^\times)^p$ is a single symbol, so the
symbol length in degree $1$ is at most $1$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_one (m p : ℕ) :
    1 ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 1 :=
  one_mem_symbolLengthBounds_one _ p

/--
**Matzri's theorem** [Matzri2016, Theorem 8.2] for $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$, which is a
$C_m$ field by Tsen–Lang [Lang1952]: for $m \ge 1$, every class in
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p^t$ is a sum of at most $t(p^{m-1} - 1)$ symbols.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 16 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p t : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) :
    t * (p ^ (m - 1) - 1) ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) (p ^ t) 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The matching lower bound in degree $2$ [BecherHoffmann2004, Proposition 4.5], by an argument going
back to Nakayama: for distinct monic irreducibles $f_1, \dots, f_{m-1}$ in $\mathbb{C}[x_1]$ the
tensor product of the symbol algebras $(f_i, x_{i+1})_p$ is a division algebra over
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$, so no $k < m - 1$ bounds the symbol length of
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 16 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two_ge (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) :
    ∀ k ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 2, m - 1 ≤ k := by
  sorry

/--
**Becher and Hoffmann's question** [BecherHoffmann2004, Question 4.6]: is the symbol length of
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$ exactly $m - 1$? Their Proposition 4.5 gives the lower
bound (`symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two_ge`), and Matzri's theorem the much weaker upper
bound $p^{m-1} - 1$ (`symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two`). For $m \le 1$ the group
vanishes and the answer is $0$; for $m = 2$ the question is whether every class is a single
symbol, which holds for $p \le 3$ by a theorem of Artin and is open for $p \ge 5$. Since $m - 1$
does not involve $p$, an affirmative answer would settle
`symbol_length_problem.variants.uniform` in degree $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 16 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two_isLeast :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ m p : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → p.Prime →
      IsLeast (symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 2) (m - 1) := by
  sorry

/--
$K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p = 0$ for $n > m$: the field has cohomological dimension $m$
[Serre1997, Ch. II, §4.2], so $H^n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m), \mu_p^{\otimes n}) = 0$, and
$K^M_n/p \cong H^n(-, \mu_p^{\otimes n})$ by the norm residue isomorphism theorem [Voevodsky2011].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.zero_mem_of_lt (m n p : ℕ) (hmn : m < n) (hp : p.Prime) :
    0 ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n := by
  sorry

/--
$K^M_n(F)/\ell = 0$ for an algebraically closed field $F$ and $n, \ell \ge 1$, since every unit
is an $\ell$-th power: every symbol $\{a_1, \dots, a_n\}$ with $a_1 = b^\ell$ equals
$\ell \{b, a_2, \dots, a_n\} = 0$. This generalizes the case $m = 0$ of
`symbol_length_problem.variants.zero_mem_of_lt`, which concerns a prime $\ell$ and the field
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_0) \cong \mathbb{C}$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 12 19]
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.isAlgClosed (F : Type*) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F]
    (n ℓ : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hℓ : 0 < ℓ) : 0 ∈ symbolLengthBounds F ℓ n := by
  rw [zero_mem_symbolLengthBounds_iff]
  refine grade_eq_bot_of_forall_exists_pow_eq F ℓ (fun a ↦ ?_) hn.ne'
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq (a : F) hℓ
  have hz0 : z ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ a.ne_zero (by rw [← hz, h, zero_pow hℓ.ne'])
  exact ⟨Units.mk0 z hz0, Units.ext (by simp [hz])⟩

end SymbolLengthMilnorKTheory

findings.description: The module docstring says Becher and Hoffmann "asked it for exactly the fields considered below (their Question 4.6)". The docstring of `degree_two_isLeast` presents its ℂ-only statement as "Becher and Hoffmann's question". But Question 4.6 is posed for F = C(X_0,…,X_m), m ≥ 1, over ANY algebraically closed field C with char C ≠ p. The Lean statement quantifies only over `MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ`, so it is the C = ℂ case of Question 4.6, not the question itself. It also adds the one-variable case m = 1, which is harmless because the value 0 is known there by Tsen. A negative answer to Becher–Hoffmann over some other algebraically closed field, e.g. one of characteristic q ≠ p, would leave the Lean statement unsettled. The file's module docstring does restrict its scope to ℂ, so this is a documented specialization. The actual slip is the claim that the source asked it for "exactly" these fields.
findings.source_evidence: Becher–Hoffmann, Homology Homotopy Appl. 6(1) (2004), p. 29: "Question 4.6. Let m be a positive integer, p a prime, and C an algebraically closed field with char(F) ≠ p. Let F = C(X_0,...,X_m) be the rational function field in m variables over C. Do we have λ_p(F) = m?" (https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/hha/2004/0006/0001/HHA-2004-0006-0001-a003.pdf)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "the case C = ℂ of their Question 4.6" (and drop "exactly the fields considered below"). Alternatively, state the general question: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (C : Type) [Field C] [IsAlgClosed C] (m p : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → p.Prime → (p : C) ≠ 0 → IsLeast (symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) C) p 2) (m - 1)`.

reformulations.difference: The answer is an `ℕ∞`-valued function `sl`, pinned down only indirectly by `∀ k : ℕ, k ∈ symbolLengthBounds … ↔ sl m n p ≤ k` rather than defined as "the least bound".
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `symbolLengthBounds F p n` is upward closed (`mem_symbolLengthBounds_of_le`). For an upward-closed S ⊆ ℕ, (∀ k, k ∈ S ↔ sl ≤ k) holds iff sl = sInf ((↑) '' S) in ℕ∞, which is the least bound when S is nonempty and ⊤ when S = ∅. That is exactly Becher–Hoffmann's symbol length λ(H) ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. So the slot asks for the true symbol length for every m, n and prime p, and the statement is satisfiable.

reformulations.difference: Becher–Hoffmann Prop. 4.5 is stated for m+1 variables X_0,…,X_m and gives λ_p ≥ m. The Lean uses `Fin m` (m variables) and bound `m - 1`, with `1 ≤ m`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is only a shift of the variable index: the file's m variables are Becher–Hoffmann's m' + 1 = m variables, so λ_p ≥ m' becomes λ_p ≥ m − 1. The case m = 1 (m' = 0) is the trivial bound 0. ℂ contains a primitive p-th root of unity, as Proposition 4.5 requires, and L = F(X_0,…,X_m) is an allowed choice of L.

reformulations.difference: Becher–Hoffmann ask "λ_p(C(X_0,…,X_m)) = m?" for m ≥ 1, i.e. at least 2 variables. The Lean asks `IsLeast (symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 2) (m - 1)` for all m ≥ 1, which also includes one variable.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Same index shift as for `degree_two_ge`. The extra conjunct m = 1 says K_2(ℂ(x))/p = 0, which is true (Tsen plus Merkurjev–Suslin), so it cannot change the answer. Because the bound set is upward closed, `IsLeast … (m-1)` is exactly λ_p = m − 1. The restriction to C = ℂ is discussed separately in findings.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. What I checked and the judgment calls I made:

1. **Definitions.** The definitions in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/FieldTheory/MilnorKTheory.lean match the sources. `RingQuot` of the Steinberg relation plus `ℓ = 0` gives T(Fˣ)/(I_St + ℓT) = K^M_*(F)/ℓ. The ideal is homogeneous, so `grade F ℓ n`, the additive closure of the degree-n symbols, is K^M_n(F)/ℓ. `symbolLengthBounds` ("every element is a sum of at most m symbols") matches Krashen's §2.1.3.4 and Becher–Hoffmann's λ. Becher–Hoffmann note that 0 is a symbol, so "l symbols" and "at most l" agree for n ≥ 1. `MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ = FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin m) ℂ)`.

2. **Lean experiments** in /workspace/review:
   - The characterization in `symbol_length_problem` is satisfiable and is equivalent to sl = the true symbol length (`sInf` in ℕ∞). Proved.
   - The t = 0 boundary of `degree_two` holds: K_2/1 = 0. Proved.
   - The `0 < n` exclusion in `uniform` is necessary: in degree 0 no k works for all primes. Proved.
   - The `answer(sorry)` slots all sit outside every quantifier, and each right-hand side has the source's polarity (not a negated form).

3. **Modelling choices, documented and defensible; not reported as findings.**
   - The file restricts Krashen's general-field Problem 2.1.3.12 to ℂ(x_1,…,x_m) and prime ℓ.
   - The main theorem asks for the exact symbol length, which is stronger than Krashen's "find a bound". Krashen's existence form is captured separately by `variants.bounded`.
   - `variants.uniform` reads Krashen's sentence "Conjecturally, however, we expect that there is a bound which doesn't depend on ℓ" as applying in every degree n ≥ 1, restricted to primes. That sentence follows the degree-2 Matzri paragraph but says "bounded in terms of ddim(k), i and ℓ", so the all-degrees reading is defensible. A degree-2-only reading would make the Lean question stronger than the source's.

4. **Docstring nits, too small to count as findings.**
   - "the survey [Krashen2016]" is a research article (arXiv:1305.5217) that introduces presentable functors; it is not a survey.
   - Krashen literally writes "no known bound on symbol length for cohomology classes of degree at least 2 over complex function fields in at least 3 variables", which contradicts his own Matzri paragraph. The file's paraphrase ("no bound is known beyond Matzri's in degree 2") is a reasonable reconciliation.

5. **Status.** No status issues.
   - Krashen (2024): the problem is "pretty wide open"; very little is known in degree ≥ 3; cyclicity is known only for ℓ ∈ {2, 3}. So Becher–Hoffmann's question for ℂ(x,y) with p ≥ 5, and bounds for odd p in degrees 3 ≤ n ≤ m, are open.
   - An arXiv/Crossref search through 2026 turned up nothing that settles `bounded`, `uniform`, `degree_two_isLeast` or the main problem. Recent papers (Chapman 2023, Matzri 2024 in Contemp. Math., Bingöl 2024, Chapman–McKinnie) treat other settings.
   - The solved tags are right: `degree_two` is Matzri's TAMS 2016 theorem plus Tsen–Lang (C_m); `degree_two_ge` is Becher–Hoffmann Prop. 4.5; `zero_mem_of_lt` follows from cd(ℂ(x_1,…,x_m)) = m plus the norm residue isomorphism.
   - The textbook items `degree_zero`, `degree_one` and `isAlgClosed` are proved in the file; `#print axioms` shows only the standard axioms, no sorry.

6. **Not read directly.** Serre, Lang, Voevodsky and Merkurjev–Suslin are standard facts used only in docstrings and in the solved statements; I relied on them without opening those sources.
